title: Manipulation of localized excitons in CrPS$_4$ by temperature and magnetic field
authors: Dipankar Jana, Swagata Acharya, Amit Pawbake, Dmitrii Litvinov, Aljoscha Soll, Zdenek Sofer, Clement Faugeras, Dimitar Pashov, Mark van Schilfgaarde, Kostya S. Novoselov, Marek Potemski, Maciej Koperski
abstract: Layered van der Waals magnetic semiconductors provide a versatile platform for exploring excitonic phenomena intertwined with spin and lattice degrees of freedom, enabling excitons to act as sensitive probes of magnetic order. CrPS$_4$ is a layered antiferromagnetic semiconductor that hosts rich excitonic features whose microscopic origin and connection to magnetic ordering remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigate the electronic and excitonic properties of bulk CrPS$_4$ using a combination of many-body perturbation theory, dynamical mean-field theory, and photoluminescence-based experiments. Our calculations establish CrPS$_4$ as a direct-gap semiconductor with a bandgap of 2.48~eV in the antiferromagnetic phase. Several sub-bandgap excitonic transitions are predicted by theory, comprising multiple spin-allowed excitons and an additional spin-flip excitation, predominantly localized on the Cr$^{3+}$ ions. Temperature- and magnetic-field-dependent optical measurements reveal thermally driven exciton redistribution among localized states and identify characteristic energy shifts that provide clear optical signatures of magnetic phase transitions in CrPS$_4$. These results provide new insights into the excitonic transitions of antiferromagnets and suggest potential routes for all-optical sensing and light-driven control of their magnetic order.
summary: The study investigates excitonic behavior in the layered antiferromagnetic semiconductor $	ext{CrPS}_4$ using both advanced theory and detailed optical measurements. Researchers found that temperature and magnetic fields induce measurable shifts in exciton energies, providing clear spectroscopic signatures of magnetic phase transitions. This work highlights the potential for all-optical control and sensing of magnetic order in these correlated materials.
main_problem: The study investigates excitonic phenomena in $	ext{CrPS}_4$, focusing on how these optical properties are intertwined with the material's spin and lattice degrees of freedom, particularly concerning magnetic ordering.
main_result: The research establishes that $	ext{CrPS}_4$ is a direct-gap semiconductor whose low-energy excitonic transitions exhibit clear, measurable energy shifts corresponding to magnetic phase transitions (AFM $\leftrightarrow$ PM).
method: A combination of advanced theoretical calculations (MBPT, DMFT, QSG$\hat{	ext{W}}$) and detailed experimental measurements (low-temperature PL/PLE spectroscopy under varying temperature and magnetic fields) was employed.
model_or_system: The system is $	ext{CrPS}_4$, a layered antiferromagnetic van der Waals semiconductor. The theoretical framework models excitons interacting with spin and lattice degrees of freedom, while experiments probe these interactions optically.
key_observables: Exciton transition energies ($\sim 1.36 	ext{ eV}$), bandgap energy ($2.48 	ext{ eV}$ in AFM phase), temperature-dependent peak shifts, and exciton decay rates ($	au$).
